# nbdev

> Write, read and review nbdev notebooks as source, documentation, examples and tests. You MUST read this before any work on a project with notebooks.

Base URL: https://nbdev.fast.ai/

notation: /why

### Source

- published library notebooks: implementation, explanation, examples, outputs, failure demos interleaved    /read top to bottom; internal project: match neighbours
- per file: `# AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT!` → edit its notebook (`# %% ../nbs/04_usage.ipynb #a45f753a` names the cell), never module, `__all__`, `_modidx.py`, module docstring    /`nbdev-export` regenerates them; unmarked: hand-written
- understand and review through notebooks and their git diff, not generated modules    /no prose, examples, tests there
- `info_md` or traceback `.py` paths in nbdev packages (siblings too): `nbrg` in `nbs/`, not exported `.py`
- notebooks teach APIs, lessons are the tests; plain `.py`, tested by `tests/*.py`: rare dense mechanism iterated under pytest; never add pytests to a project lacking them unless asked
- project questions: `nbs/index.ipynb`, README's source; after editing it: `nbdev-readme`

### Authoring

- before editing: whole notebook or every cell's summary
- new notebook: first read a role model such as claudette's `00_core.ipynb` for literate form; one of tutorial, how-to, explanation, reference; H1 title cell, `>` subtitle, intro; H2 per major concept, short narratives unsplit; each heading its own markdown cell    /Jupyter collapse
- one idea at a time: small implementation, explanation, lesson; every substantive API gets a lesson; basic functionality outside the API with little logic: usually none
- lesson: markdown intro, split when complicated; extend examples, no near-duplicates: explain the differing argument, no repeated setup; classes: `@patch` each method beside its explanation unless that obscures the API
- new behaviour worth teaching (often not, for trivial logic): choose its narrative position; lesson first, ideally by changing an existing one; run preceding cells, see it fail; intro and implementation above it, see it pass; any changed assertion likewise fails on old code, passes on new
- bug fix: make an existing example hit the failing path only for subtle logic likely to recur or a tiny readable change, else add an assertion to it; never a cell just to witness a fix; no documented behaviour change: no lesson change
- explore in the notebook, not a separate kernel, after reading existing examples; keep useful findings as lessons, delete the rest; try to leave the notebook better
- `_name`: machinery without independent contract, not everything used internally; helper useful only internally: often awkward design

### Lessons

- readability first: code and displayed output guide readers through what code does; displayed value worth testing: assign, test, show; test the point, not incidentals like formatting; errors only where readers are likely to hit them
- realistic values, minimal setup, reused objects, direct supporting assertions; `fastcore.test`, `expect_fail`, in ordinary code cells
- evidence: compact `_repr_markdown_`, structured summary, plot, table, image, HTML; large output: say what matters, store focused results
- reader-facing examples: no plumbing, mocks, dense comprehensions, long setup → small helper or hidden check
- rewrites to consider: commented example → markdown and code, keeping constraint comments; numbered steps → markdown/code pairs; `print` inside a sentence → prose or displayed value; final `print(x)` → `x`; reassignment stages, blank-line groups → introduced cells; `try`/`except` → `expect_fail`; long docstring → markdown; TODO, FIXME in example comments → resolve or issue

### Prose and exports

- markdown: rationale, distinctions, guarantees, extended explanation, examples, warnings; not code narration or filler; normally after definitions    /generated page reads correctly
- symbol docstrings short; parameters, return: docments beside signature; backticked `symbol` → nbdev link
- module docstring: `nbdev-export` joins title's `>` description and exported markdown after H1; long: one exported markdown cell per major section; shared constraints, workflows only    /`doc(module)` lists functions
- docstring beyond the default summary: only for modules read alone    /`nbdev-export` then lists module in package docs
- `#| exportd`: code cell → fenced docstring source, not module code; compact runnable demo after its definitions; preceding exported summary ends with a colon; unexported cells between: omitted
- run code before documenting a claim; `nbdev.export.nb_mdoc` previews assembly
- `index.ipynb`: export opening paragraphs    /package intro

### State and execution

- define near first use; introduce shared setup; reuse objects; never reassign names later cells use; exploration: end with an expression recording its finding, when useful
- imports: own cells, lessons too    /docs builds run import cells in fresh namespaces: mixed state-dependent code fails or runs at docs time
- outputs: generated, may be stale mid-edit; source/output mismatch: keep working, never clear by hand or edit notebook JSON; `nbdev-test --save` at PR time if outputs are kept; `--file-re`: several named notebooks in parallel

### nbdev v3 (Jan 2026)

- `#| hide`: distracting necessities; exported `_helpers` needn't be public; `#| eval: false`: must not run, not broken; later cells can't use its state
- `export`: cell metadata `{"nbdev": {"export": "true"}}` (`add_msg`/`update_msg` `export=True`, `m.meta_exported = True`); other directives as comments; `fastcore.nbio.mk_cell(...).directives` merges both, content wins; `[tool.nbdev] to_meta = ["export"]` enforces on `nbdev-clean`
- `pyproject.toml`, not `settings.ini`: `[project]` metadata, `[tool.nbdev]` settings (defaults `nbs_path='nbs'`, `doc_path='_docs'`), version via `dynamic = ["version"]` in `__init__.py`, `_modidx` in `[project.entry-points.nbdev]`
- CLIs hyphenated (`nbdev-export`, `nbdev-test`), Python names underscored; actions `fastai/workflows/nbdev3-ci`, `quarto-ghp3`
- sync, git, docs, release: `nbdev-update` (`.py` → notebooks); `nbdev-{clean,merge,install-hooks}` (clean diffs, merges); `nbdev-{docs,preview,readme}` (Quarto + GitHub Pages, LaTeX, search, auto-links); `nbdev-{release-gh,pypi,conda,changelog,bump-version}`
- `llms.txt`: generated by `nbdev-export` from `pkg/skill.py` (`doc(pyskills.createskill)`)

### Finish

- update affected prose, displays, assertions together; reread touched narrative for readability; `nbdev-test <nb>`
